extracted.intended_audience: Economists invited to referee macro submissions for Econometrica (academic referees)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for academic referees evaluating macroeconomics manuscripts submitted to Econometrica, covering timing, report structure, length, standards of evaluation, and disclosure of prior review. Emphasizes concise, prioritized actionable feedback suitable for a top journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report deadline (timeliness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Referee report must be received within SIX WEEKS (or by a reasonably close date of your choosing). Do not agree to referee if you cannot meet this deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a firm, editor-requested deadline intended to improve the publishing process. If you accept, deliver within six weeks; if you cannot, decline. The editor offers timely decisions on referees' own papers in exchange for timely reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report structure: three explicit sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly divide your report into THREE sections: Summary, Essential Points, and Suggestions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a small change: simply add the two lines 'Essential Points' and 'Suggestions' in the appropriate place of a standard referee report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary section
rubrics_metrics.description: A brief summary of how you see the contribution of the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is standard in reports; keep it concise and focused on the paper's main contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essential Points section
rubrics_metrics.description: List the points that are essential for the authors to address if the paper is to be published in a top journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include at most three items (preferably fewer). If more than three essential revisions are required, the paper should be rejected. If recommending rejection, use this section to explain the main problem(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on number of essential revisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The list of essential revisions should include at most three items, and preferably less.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a referee believes more than three essential issues exist, that indicates the paper is not suitable for revision-to-accept at a top journal and should be recommended for rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection explanation placement
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are recommending rejection, this section (Essential Points) can explain the main problem(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Essential Points to clearly state the core flaws that justify rejection rather than burying them in long discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggestions section
rubrics_metrics.description: Everything else: general suggestions for improvement and additional comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat this as the authors' paper — provide constructive suggestions. The editor views this section as including about 80% of what is in a standard referee report; it should contain helpful, non-essential recommendations that can improve the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report length expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Referee reports should not be long; two or three pages should be enough for most papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for concise, prioritized feedback rather than long exhaustive commentary. The three-section structure helps focus essential items while leaving other comments in Suggestions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of prior refereeing
rubrics_metrics.description: If you’ve refereed this paper before, bring that to the editor's attention immediately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Informing the editor of prior review history helps avoid duplication and allows the editor to interpret your evaluation in context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation standard (no narrow 'flavor')
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not look for a particular 'flavor' of paper for Econometrica: if it is good enough for the AER, it could be published in Econometrica.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate papers by general top-journal standards rather than a narrow stylistic or topical preference; Econometrica aims to compete with other top journals for the best macro papers.
